endorsements.quote: In Figure 3 , the steps for PHM use of UK-US biobanks are shown to prioritize privacy for individuals, who should understand and agree on how personal data are used for HPO well-being.

Developers must implement robust data protection measures, such as encryption and access controls, to safeguard patient information and ensure data is handled securely and transparently within a PHM ecosystem; failure to comply with these regulations could result in corrective actions, sanctions, and penalties ( Information Commissioner's Office, 2023 ).

unlisted_practices: Establish a Higher Expert Medical Science Safety (HEMSS) task force to steward classification, adoption, and adherence of AI-driven population health management tools.
Pilot HEMSS Agile Group Development programs in UK Integrated Care Board regions before expanding to US federal centers.
Have AI and digital regulation service authorities (HRA, MHRA, NICE, CQC) review, approve, and classify genome predictor and intercept AI tools as fit-for-purpose before adoption.
Use the Systems Engineering Initiative for Patient Safety (SEIPS) framework to learn from AI-related patient safety events.
Use HIMSS maturity models such as EMRAM to assess organizational digital maturity and data governance readiness for advanced AI.
Use anonymized data and citizen-informed consent for cross-border sharing of genomic data in federated learning.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/framework and policy commentary offering recommendations for population health management, AI safety stewardship (HEMSS), and governance frameworks across the US and UK.
